title: Why Is Venus 464°C While Uranus Drops to −224°C?
description:
Every Planet Explained in 12 Minutes (Mercury to Neptune)

Why is Venus 464 degrees Celsius while Uranus drops to minus 224? Rolling sideways into 21-year winters, Uranus holds an atmosphere reaching a minimum of −224.2 °C (49 K) — colder than Neptune in some places. Closer in, 92 bars of crushing air surround Venus, where a 96.5% carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat in a runaway greenhouse and bakes the rock to 464 °C (737 K).

Sources: Williams, D. R. (2024), NASA Goddard NSSDCA Venus & Uranus Fact Sheets (Venus 464 °C / 737 K surface temperature, 92 bars surface pressure, 96.5% CO2 / 3.5% N2 atmosphere; Uranus 97.77° obliquity) · NASA Science Venus Facts & Uranus Facts (runaway greenhouse effect; Uranus 21-year dark winter and 49 K / −224.2 °C minimum atmospheric temperature, colder than Neptune in some places).

Pictures: NASA/JHUAPL/NRL Parker Solar Probe WISPR, NASA SDO AIA 171, NASA/JPL Magellan (PIA00215), JAXA/ISAS/DARTS/Kevin M. Gill Akatsuki (PIA23791), NASA Pioneer Venus Orbiter, NASA/ESA/CSA JWST NIRCam (weic2332a), NASA/JPL Voyager 2 (PIA01488), and W. M. Keck Observatory Uranus imagery, with AI-assisted narration and editing. Facts: every number is checked against the sources listed above.
Image credits: NASA/JHUAPL/Naval Research Laboratory (Parker Solar Probe WISPR, SVS 14095); NASA/SDO (AIA 171 Venus Transit); NASA/JPL (Magellan SAR PIA00215, Voyager 2 PIA01488); JAXA/ISAS/DARTS/Kevin M. Gill (Akatsuki PIA23791); NASA Ames (Pioneer Venus Orbiter); NASA/ESA/CSA/STScI (JWST NIRCam weic2332a); W. M. Keck Observatory (Uranus AO cloud imagery).
